notes:
Summary:
- Account: Quantis Edge Platforms (edge inference for retail/telemetry use cases). Evaluating Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation in NA regions.
- Primary contacts: CTO Priya Rao (ML/infra), Infra lead Marcus Li, Product lead Ronan O'Leary. AE: Maya Chen; SE: Diego Morales.

Workload & performance targets (from workshop + telemetry):
- Workloads: customer-facing chat (low-latency), embeddings for semantic search, reranking pipeline for recommendation responses, periodic large-batch summarization jobs.
- Steady-state baseline: ~12 QPS for chat (avg 160-200 tokens per request) => ~2.0-2.4k tokens/sec steady.
- Peak/burst: short windows 100-140 QPS (marketing events), some requests up to 512 tokens => planning peak ~60k tokens/sec.
- Throughput goal: sustain p95 latency <= 250ms for single-turn chat under steady-state; p99 target <= 600ms for mixed workloads.
- Throughput guarantees requested: committed QPS and tokens/sec for business-critical endpoints with automatic fallback to cheaper model variants for overflow.

Model & routing preferences:
- Primary model family: quantized Llama-2 / Orca variants (13B quantized) for quality/cost balance.
- Desired fallback: 7B quantized model for overflow/burst to preserve latency/SLOs.
- Multi-model routing: prefer regional capacity (NA), failover to mid-tier models or alternate region if capacity constrained.

Dedicated sizing & reserved GPU discussion notes:
- Current Redwood proposal ask: 6 H100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool for steady state + 2 additional burst-capable GPUs (or pre-warmed instances) for event-driven spikes.
- Internal preference leaning to 8x A100-80GB (cost-conservative) vs 6x H100 (latency-optimized).
- SE recommended running continuous batching + KV cache for long-lived sessions to reduce per-token cost; suggested model quantization profile to further decrease memory footprint.
- Expected baseline utilization target: reserve capacity sized for steady-state QPS (12 QPS) + 30% headroom; burst handled via reserved burst pool or transient capacity with defined cost/latency tradeoffs.

SLA negotiation points raised by customer:
- Need formal latency SLOs per endpoint (chat vs batch) with credits for missed p95/p99 windows.
- Uptime target: 99.95% for dedicated pool; maintenance windows outside PST business hours.
- Data residency and audit: logs retained 13 months; must support KMS/HSM integration and encryption-in-transit+at-rest.
- Incident runbooks and root-cause reports within SLA timeframe.

Security/Compliance & procurement:
- Security team validated SOC2 artifact set; ISO27001 supplier certification requested.
- Legal asked for model-explainability clause and data-use language in MSA.
- Procurement: procurement lead expects final pricing + SLA by 2026-04 for Q2 budget cycle.
